The honest part

AI isn't the hard part. Wiring it into your business is.

Most owners I meet already have ChatGPT open in a tab. What they don't have is a system: the scattered notes, spreadsheets, inboxes, and calendars pulled into one place, with an assistant that keeps the whole thing moving while they run the actual business.

So that's the offer. Not software you have to figure out — a working system, built around how you already operate, set up and running.

How it works

Three steps. Then it just runs.

Step 01 — Look

We map how you run things

A working conversation about your day, your tools, and where things fall apart. No audit theater — we find the friction that costs you.

Step 02 — Build

I build your system

Your HQ, your daily cards, your follow-through — assembled on tools you control, in your name, documented as we go.

Step 03 — Run

You open one screen

Every morning: where things stand and the one next action. The system carries the rest. A few clients at a time, by design — so yours gets built properly.

The short version

Designer. Operator. The person who builds it is the person you talk to.

I'm Dale Pittman — a Denver designer and creative technologist with a hospitality decade underneath the design career. That combination is the whole point: I make complex ideas move, and I build the systems that keep them moving after the launch.

No account managers, no handoffs, no agency meter. You get the work, and the person who did it, on one thread.

One question

What are you trying to move?

A product nobody understands yet. A business running on sticky notes. A deck that has to land on Friday. Tell me what it is — I'll tell you honestly whether I'm the right build for it.
